title: Runtime error transforms and concise user guidance for SDKs
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Problem:
Developers using Redwood SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) encounter inconsistent error shapes, noisy low-level messages, and insufficient retry guidance. This leads to longer debugging cycles, broken retry logic across languages, and poor UX for streaming interruptions.

Goal:
Define a language-agnostic runtime -> SDK error transformation layer that produces:
- A small set of stable SDK error classes (TransientError, PermanentError, AuthError, PayloadError, StreamingInterrupted)
- Machine-friendly error codes (prefixed RI-ERR) and human-friendly single-line messages
- Structured retry hints surfaced consistently across languages (retryable: true/false, recommended-backoff-ms as string)
- Streaming ergonomics: resumable token guidance and clear terminal vs resumable frames

Non-goal:
We are not changing server-side HTTP codes or introducing new runtime error categories beyond mapping. Not implementing transport-level proxies here.

Proposal (high level):
1) Error model: adopt canonical fields for SDK errors: code (string), message (string), retryable (boolean-as-string), details (string) and docs_url (string). Use code namespace RI-ERR.* with stable suffixes such as RI-ERR.NETWORK_TRANSIENT, RI-ERR.AUTH_EXPIRED, RI-ERR.MODEL_MISMATCH, RI-ERR.STREAM_RESUME_REQUIRED.

2) Runtime adapter: add a thin adapter in runtime that annotates internal errors with an upstream_code and minimal telemetry keys. SDK layers will transform upstream_code -> RI-ERR.* and attach retry metadata.

3) Language SDK behavior:
- Python: raise typed exceptions (TransientError, PermanentError, AuthenticationError, PayloadError, StreamingInterrupted). Exceptions include attributes: code (str), retry_after_ms (str or None), docs_url (str), idempotency_recommendation (str).
- TypeScript: export Error subclasses with fields and a stable "type" string for easy instanceof checks. Methods to getRetryDelay() that returns recommended backoff.
- Go: return SDK error values that implement an SDKError interface with Code() string and RetryAfterMs() string. Provide helper funcs IsTransient(err error) and WrapWithContext(err, context string).

4) Streaming ergonomics:
- Define an explicit StreamingInterrupted error with a resume_token field in details (as a short base64 string). Resume token is advisory: SDK should expose it and provide a helper to rehydrate a new stream request with resume_token.
- Distinguish between terminal errors (e.g., invalid schema) vs resumable network blips. Terminal errors map to PermanentError and include a human-friendly corrective action message.

5) Retry recommendations:
- Produce backoff recommendations in the error object as RFC3339 duration string or milliseconds for easier cross-language use (we will use ms).
- Standard recommended policy in docs: for RI-ERR.NETWORK_TRANSIENT use exponential backoff 100, 300, 900 ms with jitter; for RI-ERR.RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED use linear backoff with cooldown 1000ms increments and recommend switching to lower-cost model variant.

6) Telemetry and dev experience:
- Errors should surface a docs_url linking to a human-readable KB entry with examples and remediation steps.
- Add a small SDK helper that converts raw SDK errors into a recommended log line: "[RedwoodSDK] code=RI-ERR.NETWORK_TRANSIENT retryable=true rec=300ms docs=https://redwood.ai/docs/errors#network_transient"

7) Backwards compatibility:
- Keep existing exception names for one release but emit DeprecationWarning in Python / console.warn in TypeScript when user relies on legacy error strings. Provide migration guide.

Implementation plan (tasks):
- Task A: Design canonical error mapping table (this ticket).
- Task B: Implement runtime adapter to annotate errors (runtime team). Dependency: ENG-19780 (runtime-annotate-errors).
- Task C: Implement SDK transforms for Python/TS/Go (this ticket sub-tasks).
- Task D: Add unit tests and cross-language examples (examples repo).
- Task E: Docs: error catalog and migration guide (docs).

Acceptance criteria:
- Each SDK exposes a single importable set of error classes or helpers documented in the SDK reference.
- Error objects include code + message + retry metadata + docs_url for the top 30 error types.
- Streaming interruptions provide a resume token example and at least one end-to-end test that demonstrates resume flow in Python and TS.
- CI adds lint/contract tests that fail if code namespace differs from RI-ERR.* prefix.

Examples (illustrative):
Python snippet:
try:
    resp = client.responses.create(...)
except TransientError as e:
    # e.code == 'RI-ERR.NETWORK_TRANSIENT', e.retry_after_ms == '300'
    logger.info(f"retry recommended {e.retry_after_ms}ms, docs: {e.docs_url}")
    raise

TypeScript snippet:
try {
  await client.responses.create(...)
} catch (err) {
  if (isTransientError(err)) {
    console.warn(`${err.code} retryable=${err.retryable} backoff=${err.recommendedBackoffMs}ms`)
  }
  throw err
}

Go snippet:
if err := client.Create(...); err != nil {
  if sdkerr.IsTransient(err) {
    backoff := sdkerr.RetryAfterMs(err)
    log.Printf("transient: %s backoff=%sms", sdkerr.Code(err), backoff)
  }
}

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/SDK+Error+Transforms
- Runtime PR (blocking): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4223
- Example repo PR (follow-up): https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/pull/58

Open questions:
- Should retry metadata use ms strings or integer milliseconds? (proposal: strings to avoid integer overflow in some languages; but ci contract tests will accept both if coercible)
- How strictly should SDKs enforce retryable vs. rely on application-level policies? Proposal: Surface only hints, not enforce automatic retries by default.
- Resume token size limits and safety: runtime team needs to guarantee tokens < 512 bytes base64.

Risks:
- Slight API churn for customers relying on current raw exceptions; mitigate with deprecation path.
- Inconsistent adoption across languages delayed by runtime dependency.

Rollback plan:
- Revert SDK transforms in the release if telemetry shows increased customer errors > 2x during canary.
